sections.overview: Nannacara anomala is a small Guianan freshwater cichlid known both from coastal river systems in northeastern South America and the aquarium trade.
sections.identification: Adult males grow larger and develop brighter colours and longer unpaired fins, while females are smaller and show a dark lateral stripe that becomes a checkerboard pattern when spawning.
sections.habitat: It inhabits freshwater rivers of Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana and is often recorded in seasonally flooded coastal savannas.
sections.diet: Species summaries report a varied small-prey diet including worms, crustaceans and insects.
sections.behavior: In social groups males form a dominance hierarchy, while a breeding female can become strongly territorial around her eggs and fry.
sections.reproduction: The female deposits up to about 300 eggs on a cleaned surface and guards both eggs and fry, a form of substrate brood care documented in laboratory studies.
sections.ecology: This species belongs to the same genus as Nannacara aureocephalus, whose profile covers a more restricted French Guianan range; N. anomala is recorded across several Guianan river systems.
sections.conservation: FishBase relays a global IUCN Least Concern assessment dated 12 March 2023; that category does not establish that every local habitat is unchanged.
